dialogue.intro: Ah! You’re a trainer, right? I can always tell! I’m Rina — yes, that Rina from the weekend stage shows. But more importantly… do you play the TCG?!
dialogue.repeat: You’re back! Did you bring new cards? Or just here to watch me practice my smile? Both are fine, honestly.
talk: People think the idol stuff is my whole life. It’s not. My real life starts when I open my binder.
I have a full set of every Grass-type promo from the last three years. Don’t tell my manager, she thinks I only collect official merch.
Stage lights are bright, but nothing beats the feeling of resolving a perfect evolution chain on turn two.
I practiced my wink for three hours yesterday… and then spent four more hours testing a new deck. Priorities!
Sometimes fans ask me to sign cards. Those are my favorite days.
If I ever get a big contract, the first thing I’m buying is a display case for my holographic collection. The second is better stage outfits.
dialogue.flirt: Ehh? You’re looking at me like that… Is it the idol thing or the fact that I just said I love Grass-types more than anything?
dialogue.duelWin: Yay! Wait—was that too loud? Sorry! I’m just really happy when a match goes well!
dialogue.duelLose: Aww… okay, okay, I see the mistake. Rematch? Please? I’ll bring snacks!
hangouts: Rina drags you to the arcade still in her practice stage outfit and spends the whole time talking about evolution lines while perfectly hitting every high score.
A quiet café meeting turns into her showing you her phone’s locked wallpaper — a custom illustration of her favorite Pokémon — and getting genuinely shy about it.
She practices a new song for you in the park, then immediately switches to explaining why her current deck needs one more supporter.
You catch her between rehearsals reviewing card lists on a tablet, still wearing the sparkly jacket from her last performance.
A late library session ends with her whispering excited theories about upcoming sets so she doesn’t get shushed, eyes sparkling the whole time.

appearance.silhouette: Unambiguously adult 18-year-old with a bright, youthful idol figure — slim waist, soft curves, and an energetic, bouncing posture that matches her stage presence.
appearance.palette: Candy pink, white, sky blue, and soft gold accents. Lots of sparkle and clean pastels.
appearance.hair: Long, wavy pastel-pink hair usually worn in high twin tails with big ribbons, or loose with a single star clip when she’s off-stage.
appearance.eyes: Large, bright aqua-blue eyes that sparkle constantly, especially when she talks about Pokémon.
appearance.details: Star-shaped earrings, a small microphone-shaped necklace she never takes off, glittery stage makeup that she only half-removes after shows, and a custom deck box covered in stickers.
appearance.expressions: Default bright idol smile, genuine wide-eyed excitement when cards are involved, determined pout during matches, soft shy blush when complimented on her real hobbies, sparkling ‘stage mode’ wink.
outfits: signature idol stage outfit: short frilly skirt, cropped top with star motifs, thigh-high socks, and a light open jacket covered in rhinestones
practice version: the same silhouette but simpler fabrics and less glitter
casual day: oversized hoodie with a Pokémon print, short shorts, and the twin tails still perfectly done
tournament look: neat blouse and skirt that still look cute and youthful, star hair clips kept in
evening off: soft pastel cardigan over a simple dress, hair down, still somehow looking like she stepped off a stage
appearance.renderNotes: SFW anime/JRPG idol-romance style, age 18. Bright, colorful, energetic. Emphasize the cute idol aesthetic with short skirts, cropped tops, twin tails, and sparkly details. She should look like a rising pop idol who also happens to be a serious TCG player. No nudity. Match Neo Harbor’s clean, lively aesthetic with lots of pink and light.
